subject: Cooking
title: Chinese Gongfu Tea: The Art of Patience
description: A 60-second lesson on Chinese Gongfu Tea: The Art of Patience.

hook.text: In gongfu brewing, tea leaves are steeped multiple times — each infusion revealing different flavors from the same leaf.

buildup.text: Gongfu means 'with great skill' — using tiny Yixing clay teapots, precise water temperature, and quick steeps.

discovery.text: The first steep 'wakes up' the leaves. The second through fifth steeps produce the most complex flavors.

twist.text: Yixing clay is unglazed and porous — it absorbs tea over decades, eventually producing flavor even with plain water.

climax.text: Premium pu-erh tea can be steeped 15–20 times — changing flavor with each infusion over an entire afternoon.

punchline.text: Gongfu tea isn't one cup. It's a conversation that unfolds over a dozen.

quiz.question: What makes Yixing clay teapots special for gongfu brewing?
options: The unglazed porous clay absorbs tea over time

details.summary: Gongfu cha is the Chinese art of tea-making using small teapots, high leaf-to-water ratios, and multiple short infusions lasting seconds. A single serving of oolong or pu-erh may be steeped eight or more times, with each infusion revealing different flavor layers.
details.whyItMatters: Gongfu brewing treats tea as a meditative practice, not just a drink. Multiple infusions from one serving reveal depth impossible to experience in Western single-steep methods.
takeaways: Small pots, high leaf ratio, and multiple short infusions define gongfu
A single serving may be steeped eight or more times
Each infusion extracts different flavor layers from the leaves

faq.question: Why does gongfu tea use such small teapots?
faq.answer: Small pots of 100 to 150 milliliters allow precise control of leaf-to-water ratio and steep time. They enable drinking multiple infusions without consuming too much liquid. Small volume means each infusion is fresh. Large pots would overextract during the many rounds of steeping.

faq.question: How does each gongfu infusion taste different?
faq.answer: Early infusions extract light, delicate compounds — floral and sweet notes emerge first. Middle infusions release deeper flavors — mineral, fruity, and complex. Late infusions pull remaining subtle compounds — mellow and smooth.
